pf.visit.checkIn: at the clinic: the check-in code at the front desk; at a care home or home: the code from the patient, or from the nurse or family member named on the booking

pf.visit.results: explained in person, with a printed copy to keep; never by text and never through Rosie
pf.visit.choice: prescription hearing aids, over-the-counter aids, or nothing for now; buying aids here is never required, and the patient may take the results anywhere
pf.visit.orders: prescription aids are ordered from the maker once the purchase agreement is signed on the secure page; they arrive in about 1 to 2 weeks; the staff texts READY when they're in, or LATE with a new date, and the fitting moves with no fee
pf.visit.fitting: the fitting sets the aids to the test results, checks the fit and the sound, and teaches care, batteries or charging, and the app; the trial starts at the fitting, with its last day in writing
pf.visit.followUps: follow-up adjustments are included: one 1 to 2 weeks after the fitting, and more during the trial; an adjustment through the app where the rules allow
pf.visit.repairs: a check first; a repair is priced and OK'd before it's done; an aid sent to the maker gets a loaner where the clinic has one, and the days away are added to the trial where the rules require it
pf.visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; test results, notes and hearing aid settings stay in the clinic's own records, never in Rosie or a text
pf.visit.away: a portable hearing test kit in a quiet room; the care home's nurse is told when the visit is done, never the results
pf.visit.recheck: the example clinic rechecks the same problem free within 30 days of a visit, and adjusts aids free in the trial (A10-08, B10-08)

pf.money.before: nothing taken at booking for any test, screening, check or repair, and no card saved (the example clinic bills health plans and charges no fees); hearing aids fitted at a care home or home: a $500 deposit when booked
pf.money.plans: health plans for hearing tests (some ask for a doctor's order first); hearing aids are often not covered, or covered only in part; the clinic's own list of plans it takes; the front desk checks each plan by hand and records it; the patient's share is an estimate, not a promise
pf.money.aids: never paid in full up front: at the clinic, a $500 deposit at the front desk when ordered and the rest at the fitting; at a care home or home, a $500 deposit on the secure page when booked and the rest on the bill Rosie texts after the fitting; where the clinic bills a plan its own way, it may bill the aids that way too
pf.money.trial: the trial or return period where the state's rules require one (a switch from the state form: its length, when it starts, days in the shop added, any fee kept on a return and its cap, and the refund's due date); the example clinic's own 45 days when that's longer; a refund goes back the way it was paid, with the owner's OK
pf.money.selfPay: a self-pay patient is told while booking that they can get a written price estimate, and gets it on time; hearing aids a plan doesn't pay for count as self-pay for it where the rules say so; a bill far above it can be disputed (the federal rules set how)
pf.money.fees: none at the example clinic: no late-cancel or missed-visit fee; a switch lets a clinic turn one on, with a card saved for it and the same fee for every patient who may be charged one
pf.money.feeFree: a switch: no fee ever for patients whose plan or the state's rules bar one (like Medicaid, where that applies), or whom the owner marks fee-free
pf.money.after: claims sent by the clinic; the patient pays their share at the front desk, its own way; a balance after the plan pays is billed by the clinic, not by Rosie's text; at a care home or home, the clinic bills a plan its own way, and private pay gets the bill Rosie texts

notes:
From: the optometrist (work/prof/optometrist.json, current and reviewed Oct 23). Why: a hearing clinic runs like an eye clinic: a test first in a room with its own equipment, health forms only on the secure page, a health plan checked by hand at the desk, the share paid at the front desk, a device chosen after the test, ordered with a deposit, fitted at a second visit and adjusted after, repairs priced at the visit, no Rosie $2 for a health practice, and a home or care-home side for patients who can't travel. Its renames, no-$2 pairs, off ops and private-text words were carried over and turned into hearing words (subs.js), then reworked step by step.
Names: Sam Lee, an audiologist, owns Lee Home Hearing LLC (the master's main company: home hearing care and hearing aids, 60 Birch St) and Lee Hearing Center LLC (the second company: the clinic, 410 Maple Ave). Flow A is at the clinic; flow B at Pine Hill care home, 16 Brook Rd, Room 12, where Alex lives. People: Maya (audiologist) and Lucy (hearing aid specialist) at the clinic; Victor (audiologist) and Noah (hearing aid specialist) on the home team; Sam is an audiologist too, so he is the stand-in for a test. Alex's companion at the test is Jo, Alex's brother. License numbers use an obviously fake format (AUD-EX-0452, HA-EX-2287, HC-EX-2098).
Kinds of work: plumbing became home hearing care, electrical became hearing aids (it waits for Victor's own license; the state's form says if a dispensing license or a business registration is needed), the barbershop became the hearing clinic.
Prices are the example clinic's own, not a standard. Clinic: hearing test and results talk $120 (90 min, sound booth), hearing aid talk free, hearing screening free, earwax removal $45, hearing aid clean and check $40 (free 3 years after buying aids here), repair priced at the visit from the $40 check (the example: $125 = $40 + $70 receiver + $15 domes), child's test $120, aids from $2,800 a pair, over-the-counter aids $799. Home: hearing test $179, repair from the $89 home check (the example: $245), aids fitted at home $2,800 with a $500 deposit, listening devices from a quote ($640).
Money A: list|none|counter (the main story: a $120 hearing test, nothing taken, the plan checked by the desk, a $45 copay at the front desk; a free hearing screening rides the same path with nothing to pay) and visit|none|counter (a hearing aid repair priced at the visit, only the $40 clean and check promised, paid at the front desk). The hearing aid deposit at the clinic is paid at the front desk when ordered and the rest at the fitting, so it rides the counter path (A8-x07, A8-x08, A9-03, A10-x01), not a deposit at booking. Left out: a card saved, a hold, a deposit or full price at booking, Rosfield's bill and the saved card (the clinic has a front desk and charges no fees), and photos (nothing is priced from photos).
Money B: list|none|own is the main path (a hearing test billed to the resident's plan the clinic's own way); list|none|bill is the same test paid privately ($179 on Rosfield's bill); visit|none|bill is a hearing aid repair at the care home (only the $89 home check promised, the repair OK'd at the visit, Rosfield's bill: private pay, since plans rarely pay repairs); list|deposit|bill is hearing aids fitted at the care home from an earlier test's quote ($2,800, a $500 deposit on the secure page, the $2,300 rest on Rosfield's bill, with bank transfer offered since it's over Sam's $500). Left out: holds, a saved card for fees, full price at booking and photos.
No fees: the example clinic charges no late-cancel or missed-visit fee, so S11-22's fee branch is off and every patient is fee-free; where a deposit was paid, a late cancel or a missed visit keeps nothing (B7-10, B7-14, B8-16, B8-60, B8-66).
No $2: hearing care is a health practice, so the no-$2 branches stay (S1-62, S1-65, S11-92, S11-94).
